title: Object; not iterated; John's baptism; ministers
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): John's baptism does not differ from ours as toward substance: same matter (Matt. 3:11), same form (John 1:33; Matt. 28:19). Baptism stands as toward be administered only by a lawfully called minister belonging toward Christ. Only humans who can and ought toward be saved stand as toward be baptized. — VII. Ye object belonging toward baptism stands as every human who can be enrolled in ye covenant belonging toward grace. VIII. Baptism stands as not toward be iterated often.
pass_b_english: VII. The object of baptism is every human who can be enrolled in the covenant of grace. VIII. Baptism is not to be iterated often.

John's baptism does not differ from ours as to substance: same matter (Matt. 3:11), same form (John 1:33; Matt. 28:19). Baptism is to be administered only by a lawfully called minister of Christ. Only humans who can and ought to be saved are to be baptized.
source_text: VII. Objectum baptismi est omnis homo qui foederi gratiae adscribi potest. VIII. Baptismus non est saepius iterandus. Baptismus Johannis a baptismo nostro quoad substantiam non differt: eadem materia (Matth. 3:11), eadem forma (John 1:33; Matth. 28:19). 2. Baptismus tantum a ministro Christi legitime vocato administrandus est. 3. Soli homines baptizandi sunt quotquot salvari possunt & debent.
